steps.python_approach: pd.read_csv(csv_path) keeping the default RangeIndex (raw 0-based row position); rename columns with an explicit make.names helper (invalid characters other than alphanumerics, '.' and '_' become '.') so 'default payment next month' -> 'default.payment.next.month'. Never sort/reset_index.
df.columns = [c.lower() for c in df.columns], applied after make.names.
df.loc[df['education'].isin([0,4,5,6]), 'education'] = 4 on the numeric column, before the marriage recode (R order).

Positions 6..11 resolved (after id removal) to names ['pay_0','pay_2','pay_3','pay_4','pay_5','pay_6']; loop over these names: cast to float (R numeric) and df.loc[df[col].isin([-2,-1,0]), col] = 0.0. No iloc.

Keep the codes; the public design_matrix(df) builds treatment dummies explicitly from the captured xlevels (sex [1,2], education [1,2,3,4], marriage [1,2,3]): column '<var><level>' = (code == level) for every non-reference level. No get_dummies.
TARGET = 'default.payment.next.month' kept numeric 0/1 (event indicator; R levels '0','1'); y = (value != first level '0') as float.
caret removed. No split code: fit() receives the train rows chosen by the harness from the R capture.

TERMS = R coefficient names with '(Intercept)' first; design_matrix(df) returns exactly these float columns. numpy IRLS mirroring glm.fit: mustart=(y+0.5)/2, eta=logit(mustart), logit clamps as R, deviance-based stop |dev-devold|/(|dev|+0.1) < 1e-8, maxit=25; WLS via QR; SEs from the R factor of the last iteration's weighted QR, dispersion 1. fit returns a dict incl. iterations and converged. coefficients() returns term/estimate/std_error with R names.
X_new = design_matrix(df) (same captured levels); return logit-inverse of X_new @ beta; NaN where any input is missing (none in this data).

steps.r_construct: sex, education, marriage used as model inputs
steps.python_approach: Migrated faithfully without removal or change; recorded as protected attributes for validation.
